newsitem.title: UK: RTZ,human rights activists lock horns.
newsitem.headline: RTZ,human rights activists lock horns.

text.p: Activists and RTZ Corp Plc locked horns on Wednesday over human rights and environmental issues at the annual shareholders meeting of the UK arm of Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ-CRA.

At a sometimes tumultuous meeting, activist shareholders from lobby groups such as the Friends of the Earth and the World Development Movement accused RTZ-CRA of ignoring indigenous people living near mining developments.
RTZ responded by saying it was strongly committed to developing good relationships with local communities.
Chairman Bob Wilson pointed at various measures taken such as investments in healthcare projects to achieve its goal.

Activists, however, asked for RTZ-CRA to withdraw from projects such as the major Grasberg copper and gold mine in the Indonesian province of Irian Jaya. The remote province has seen several outbreaks of civil unrest in recent years.
RTZ-CRA has an 11 percent interest in Grasberg, which is managed by PT Freeport Indonesia, which in turn is majority owned by U.S. company Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc.
Activist dissatisfaction reached its peak when several shareholders loudly protested Wilson's decision to stop taking further questions more than two hours into the meeting.
RTZ shareholders had earlier voted on having their company's name changed into Rio Tinto Plc.
The result, however, will only be known when CRA shareholders will also have voted on the matter at their meeting in Australia later this month.
